name: Saudi Arabia

languages.note: Multinational and giga-project tech teams commonly work in English; Arabic is valued for government-facing roles (general observation, not sourced).

salary.note: low = Jooble senior developer Riyadh ~SAR 19,877/month x 12 (posting-based); high = Levels.fyi Riyadh senior SWE total-comp upper value SAR 420,232/year (median SAR 343,798, updated 2026-04-01; skews to large tech employers and includes bonus/stock). PayScale early-career senior average ~SAR 15,000 (period unclear). Packages usually include housing and transport allowances. Approximate, low confidence.

income_tax_note: No personal income tax on employment income (general knowledge, not re-verified this session); expat costs include monthly levies on dependents (reported SAR 400/dependent/month, unverified) and 15% VAT (not re-verified).
cost_of_living_note: Dependent levy materially raises family cost of living; no sourced housing figures gathered.

visa_routes.name: Employer-sponsored work visa and iqama (skill-based classification)

salary_threshold.note: From 2025-08-03 new hires are classified high-skilled / skilled / basic. High-skilled = occupation groups 1-3, minimum wage + professional accreditation + points test (education, experience, wage; Vialto adds skills and age). Official wage/points figures not found; one consultancy cites SAR 15,000 and >=70 points (unverified).

visa_routes.degree_requirement: Attested degree matching the visa profession. Professional Accreditation programme: 'Professional Verification' (qualification check) for high-skill jobs; India was among the first five countries covered and it now spans 160 countries. Engineering professions on the iqama require Saudi Council of Engineers (SCE) registration.
visa_routes.three_year_indian_bachelors_note: Risky for an 'Engineer' visa title: SCE assesses whether the academic programme qualifies for the engineer title (anecdotal reports say 8-semester/4-year degrees are expected). SCE also links IT iqama professions such as 'Software Development Specialist' and 'Software Engineering Specialist' to SCE registration at specialist/technician level. A BCA holder should seek a non-engineer title (e.g. programmer/developer/specialist) agreed with the employer before the visa is issued. Unconfirmed officially.
visa_routes.lottery_or_quota: No lottery. Nitaqat Saudization quotas by sector/profession; MHRSD announced higher Saudization for engineering and procurement roles (2026-01-04) and a next phase of 'Developed Nitaqat' (2026-04-26). Whether IT/software roles are directly affected was not confirmed. Basic tier has an age limit of 60 (not relevant to high-skilled).
visa_routes.path_to_pr: No standard PR; Premium Residency (incl. Special Talent) is the long-term route.
visa_routes.employer_cost_note: Employer pays the expat work-permit levy, reported as SAR 800/month per expat where expats outnumber Saudis (SAR 700 otherwise) plus a SAR 100/year work-permit service fee - aggregator figures, unverified.

visa_routes.name: Premium Residency - Special Talent (5-year)

salary_threshold.note: Healthcare and science professionals at whitelisted entities: SAR 35,000/month, bachelor's or higher, 3+ years experience. Researchers SAR 14,000; executives SAR 80,000. Per Fragomen/Centuro; official page not read.

visa_routes.degree_requirement: Bachelor's or higher (healthcare/science category); employer must be a whitelisted entity (3,484 private-sector entities reported approved).
visa_routes.three_year_indian_bachelors_note: Unclear whether a 3-year bachelor's is accepted; and whether software roles count as 'science professionals' is unconfirmed.
visa_routes.path_to_pr: 5-year permit, renewable; holders may become eligible for permanent Premium Residency if residency requirements are met (secondary sources).

sponsor_register.name: No public sponsor register (Nitaqat status visible only via logged-in Qiwa)
sponsor_register.how_to_use: Any licensed establishment with available Nitaqat visa quota may sponsor; the app cannot check this logged-out. Premium Residency whitelisted-entity list not found publicly.

negative: candidates currently in the country only

ease_for_indian_nationals.rationale: Large and growing tech hiring with high pay and English-speaking teams, and Indians are a core expatriate workforce. Friction: Saudization quotas, the 2025 skill-based classification and professional verification, SCE rules on 'engineer' titles that disadvantage a 3-year BCA, and employer levies that make employers selective.

factors.degree_recognition: Professional verification of qualifications; SCE engineer-title assessment is likely to reject 3-year degrees for 'Engineer' titles (anecdotal).
factors.employer_willingness: Moderate-high for senior tech; levies raise the bar.
factors.attestation_or_paperwork: Degree attestation plus Professional Accreditation verification; visa title must match qualification.

relocation_norms: Employer-paid visa and iqama are standard; packages commonly include housing and transport allowances. Flights, schooling and who pays dependent levies vary and were not sourced.

communities.note: Threads on iqama profession changes and SCE registration.

scam_warnings: Check that the visa profession (iqama title) printed on the offer matches your degree; a mismatched 'engineer' title can block SCE registration and iqama renewal.
Jadarat is for Saudi nationals only; offers claiming to come 'through Jadarat' for expatriates are suspect.
Any request for money (visa fee, processing fee, 'deposit', medical or 'security' fee) before or after an offer is a red flag; MOHRE states genuine employers cover all recruitment costs.
Offers that ask you to travel or start work on a visit/tourist visa: visit visas do not permit work; India's MEA says a genuine offer must allow emigration on an employment/work visa.

Unregistered Indian recruiting agents: MEA advisories report job seekers cheated by unregistered agents, with overcharging of roughly Rs 2-5 lakh; check the agent's licence number on the eMigrate 'List of active RA' (https://emigrate.gov.in/ext/raList.action).
A genuine overseas offer (per MEA) carries an employment contract signed by the foreign employer, the recruitment agent and the worker.
MEA (Aug 2023) warned that some agents misused foreign employers' eMigrate logins to generate fake offers, so an eMigrate-looking document alone is not proof.

App-detectable signals: fee/deposit keywords ('processing fee', 'visa charges', 'refundable deposit'), free-mail recruiter domains (gmail/yahoo/outlook) claiming to be a large company, WhatsApp/Telegram-only contact, no company name or address, salary far above market, 'immediate hiring, no interview', early requests for passport scans or bank details, and 'free visa' / 'visa for sale' wording ('فيزا حرة', 'إقامة حرة').
